stories.title: S1: Splash handoff fix -- readiness = Pi-core-up, not vehicle-connected (splash reaches the dashboard)
stories.completionNotes:
ROOT CAUSE was TWO coupled defects, and fixing either alone leaves the splash pinned. (1) The WIRING: eclipse-boot-state.service constructs BootStateEmitter with only statesDir+hardCapSeconds, so obdProbeFn fell to `lambda: OBD_STARTING` -- a claim that checks are IN PROGRESS, permanently false. (2) The COUPLING: that never-terminal tier GATED the handoff, capping progress at 2/3 so healthy never went true -> boot-state-poll.js never called window.close() -> splash-boot.service's OnSuccess=eclipse-dashboard.service never fired; after the 12s cap it degraded to the literal 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)' and held until reboot.

FIX. CORE_SERVICES_DEFAULT = eclipse-states-http + eclipse-powerwatch + boot-progress-finalize (all plain systemctl), plus the dashboard assets being installed. eclipse-obd moved to INFORMATIONAL_SERVICES_DEFAULT -- still sampled, still reported, never gating. Added OBD_NOT_PROBED ('not-probed') as the default when no tier probe is injected: same lesson as US-492's `unknown`-vs-guard-down finding, a reading NOT TAKEN must never be rendered as a state. The obdProbeFn injection seam is preserved and still non-gating, per the story's conditionalOutcome.

PAYLOAD SHAPE CHANGED -- read this before building S3/US-496 or any vehicle-slice card. `services` now carries ONLY `systemctl is-active` strings; it no longer overwrites the eclipse-obd entry with a tier verdict. The tier moved to its own top-level `obdTier` field (one fact per field, per specs/ssot-design-pattern.md). New fields: `obdTier`, `coreServices` (the gate's membership, so a consumer can see WHAT gated), `uiAssets` ('present'|'missing'). Verified by grep that the only external consumer is boot-state-poll.js, which reads healthy/degraded/degradedReason/progress only -- so nothing on the render side needed a change. No JS was touched.

JUDGEMENT CALL worth PM/Atlas review: I made missing dashboard assets a DEGRADE (holds the splash, reason 'dashboard assets not installed') rather than merely not-healthy. AC-1 names 'dashboard assets present' as part of readiness, and handing off to a dashboard that was never installed IS the A-16 blank screen -- so this converts a silent blank screen into a loud named message. A failed core unit outranks it in the one-line degradedReason (the more fundamental fault wins).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: I did not gate on the Pi-local emitters (system-status/battery-health/light), though design §5 S1 mentions 'states server + Pi-local emitters'. Those run under the orchestrator inside eclipse-obd.service -- gating on them would smuggle the vehicle coupling straight back in through the side door. AC-1's narrower wording (states_http + dashboard assets) is the correct gate and is what I built.

TESTING NOTE for whoever writes US-499 (S6): extracted buildEmitter() so the PRODUCTION WIRING is assertable. This mattered -- no test of computeBootState in any shape could have caught this bug, because computeBootState was always correct; the defect was a dependency the entry point silently never passed. test_main_wiresTheCoreOnlyGate asserts on the emitter main() actually hands runForever. Likewise test_emitter_uiAssetProbe_readsTheRealAssetPath PERTURBS the file on disk rather than asserting a value, so it proves the probe reads the path (US-492's 'test the wiring, not the coincidence' lesson).

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 172 passed / 1 skipped in tests/pi/splash (22 in the rewritten boot-state module), 100 passed in tests/deploy/test_deploy_pi.py + tests/pi/ops (touched the unit file + the manifest's units), ruff clean on both touched Python files. HOST GAPS unchanged from Sprint 64: `make`, black and mypy are not installed on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly. PM: the story asks for 'Typecheck green', so please run mypy at integration time; the module gained typed params (Callable[[], bool], str|None) but was not type-checked here.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10): specs/architecture.md 'F-103 Splash Subsystem' updated in-sprint -- the unit table row plus a new 'Readiness contract' subsection stating the gate membership, why eclipse-obd is excluded, and the NOT_PROBED-vs-STARTING distinction. Also corrected the deploy/eclipse-boot-state.service header, which still described the old critical-set gate, and documented why Wants= (not Requires=) eclipse-states-http is correct now that states-http is a gate member: the instrument must survive the failure it reports.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-4 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box. Both validationCriteria are on-Pi: (a) bench-boot the Pi with NO car and confirm the splash reaches healthy and hands off to eclipse-dashboard rather than pinning at 'not ready (starting)'; (b) curl the boot-state after boot and confirm healthy:true, obdTier:'not-probed', uiAssets:'present'. Do (b) FIRST -- if uiAssets reads 'missing' the splash will now hold with 'dashboard assets not installed', which is the honest report of a real stale-/opt condition (exactly what US-495's force-refresh addresses), NOT a regression of this story. Note the fix takes effect on the next boot; a mid-deploy restart of eclipse-boot-state.service is enough to re-check (b) without rebooting.

stories.title: S2: Overlay [hidden] CSS guard + /opt asset force-refresh (kill the dead overlapping DTC takeover)
stories.completionNotes:
TWO DEFECTS, ONE STORY -- and they are the same defect wearing different clothes: something was only ever ADDED and never SUBTRACTED, so a retired thing kept winning.

(1) THE CSS. Confirmed Atlas's root cause exactly, and found ONE MORE offender than the five he listed: #dtc-ribbon is a sixth, and it is the nastiest, because it also runs `animation: ribbon-pulse 2s infinite` -- an unhidden ribbon pulses a phantom alert band across every card at idle, which is a direct F-6 no-phantom violation, not just clutter. FIX is the global `[hidden] { display: none !important; }`. The !important is LOAD-BEARING, not defensive: an ID selector already outranks any plain [hidden] rule we could write, so the guard has to win on IMPORTANCE or be duplicated onto every element -- and the next overlay someone adds would ship the bug again. Documented the consequence in the CSS: an element that needs to be present-but-invisible must NOT use `hidden` (use aria-hidden + visibility). No JS touched; Iris's JS was correct throughout, and it uses `el.hidden` exclusively (grep-verified, 18 call sites).

TEST -- and this is the part worth reading. I did NOT grep the stylesheet for the guard string. tests/ui/test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py enumerates every element the SHIPPED MARKUP carries `hidden` on, then resolves the winning `display` through a miniature cascade (importance -> specificity -> source order, with a real compound-selector matcher). So it is data-driven from the artifact: an overlay added next sprint is covered the day it is added, and the guard cannot be quietly deleted. It went RED naming all six offenders and their exact winning selectors. FIDELITY LIMIT, stated in the file for US-499/S6 to pick up: only compound simple selectors are matched -- a combinator or an unresolvable pseudo-class is skipped, and skipping a `display` rule makes the test LENIENT (falsely green), not falsely red. A true CSS-cascade render is S6's job; this is the static contract S6 will exercise for real. Also pinned the inverse (each overlay STILL declares display:flex when NOT hidden) -- the cheap way to pass the guard test is to delete `display: flex`, which would centre nothing and break every overlay's layout.

(2) THE STALE /opt. Diagnosed before fixing: 'ODB2' appears NOWHERE in this repo (repo-wide grep, zero hits), so the Pi was serving a file from a generation that no longer exists in source. The mechanism: both asset steps only ever installed ON TOP of /opt and NOTHING was ever pruned, and eclipse-states-http searches `--assets-dir /opt/splash` BEFORE `/opt/dashboard` -- so one forgotten file in /opt/splash SHADOWS the real asset in /opt/dashboard permanently, and the dashboard step, which only writes to /opt/dashboard, can never dislodge it. `install -m 0644` overwriting was never the problem; the absence of deletion was.

FIX: deploy/asset-refresh.sh -> refresh_asset_dir SRC DST MANIFEST [KEEP]. Install the manifest, PRUNE everything the repo cannot vouch for (including a MANIFEST asset the source kit no longer ships -- an honest 404 beats a confident stale render), then VERIFY byte-for-byte with cmp. Both steps delegate to it. KEEP-LIST exists for one reason: /opt/splash has TWO installers (this step ships 3 served assets + version.txt; the kit's own install.sh ships the SVGs + shutdown surface). Pruning to only what THIS step installs would delete the other installer's work mid-deploy, and an A-9 skip of the kit step would then leave the Pi with NO splash -- a worse failure than the stale one being fixed. /opt/dashboard has a single installer, so no keep-list, and anything else there is pruned.

DELIBERATE POSTURE CHANGE vs A-9, PM/ATLAS PLEASE REVIEW: ABSENCE still warns-and-continues (a Pi without the UI kit ships the rest of the tier -- unchanged). A FAILED WRITE now BLOCKS the deploy (non-zero, and `set -e` aborts). Those are different facts: absence is a Pi that was never given a UI; a failed write is a deploy that BELIEVES it shipped one and did not. Continuing past the second is exactly what prints 'Deploy OK' over a stale surface and sends the operator to debug the UI instead of the deploy -- the A-16 lesson. Note the abort lands before step_restart_service, so a blocked deploy is a half-deploy; I judged a loud half-deploy better than a silent stale one, but that is the CIO's call to overrule.

WHY A LIBRARY FILE and not inline in the remote heredoc: it makes the logic ACTUALLY TESTABLE. tests/deploy/test_asset_refresh.py sources the SAME shell function that runs on the Pi (it is rsynced there by sync_tree) and drives it against temp dirs with ASSET_SUDO= -- real behaviour, not a grep of deploy-pi.sh. 7 behavioural tests incl. the shadow-prune, the keep-list, A-9 absence, and a failed write (the `install` binary shimmed to a no-op through PATH, so the production path is untouched and only the system tool underneath is neutered). Plus 4 WIRING tests on deploy-pi.sh's real step bodies -- last story's lesson, one story old: a correct routine nobody calls is worth nothing, and no test of the routine can tell you it is not called.

CHECKED AND CLEAN, no action needed: the SPLASH kit does not have the same CSS defect (#degraded-msg / #amber-ring declare no `display`, so the UA [hidden] rule applies unopposed) -- so no TD filed. carousel.js reads NO element geometry anywhere (grepped getBoundingClientRect/offset*/client*), so hiding six previously-always-rendered elements cannot perturb layout math.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): tests/ui 200 passed (8 new); tests/deploy 325 passed / 1 skipped (11 new, incl. the full deploy-pi.sh bash smoke test that forks ~10 dry-run invocations); `bash -n` clean on both shell files; ruff clean on both new test files. Also ran `bash deploy/deploy-pi.sh --dry-run` and read the two asset steps' output to confirm the wiring renders the right SRC/DST/manifest/keep-list. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprint 64/65): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly. PM: story asks 'Typecheck green'; the only Python I added is test files, but please run mypy at integration time.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10) met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md F-092 section gained (a) a 'Surface invariant: hidden means NOT RENDERED' subsection explaining why the !important is load-bearing, and (b) an '/opt asset-ownership contract' subsection with the manifest/keep-list table, the search-order shadowing hazard, and the A-9 posture change.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-4 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box, all three validationCriteria are on-Pi. Order matters: run the DEPLOY first and READ ITS OUTPUT -- the refresh now PRINTS every pruned file. Those 'pruned stale asset X' lines ARE the diagnosis of the 25-day mystery; capture them before they scroll. Then with no DTC, load the dashboard (expect: no overlay paints, carousel clean + clickable), trigger one overlay (expect: only that one, dismissable), and check the wordmark reads 'ECLIPSE OBD-II'. NOTE ON THE WORDMARK: it is the SPLASH's #wordmark (splash-pi/index.html), NOT a dashboard top-bar element -- the dashboard top bar has no wordmark in this generation, which is itself corroboration that the Pi is rendering a retired generation. If the wordmark still reads 'ODB2' AFTER a deploy whose output shows no prune and a clean verify, then the stale copy is NOT in /opt and the next place to look is the chromium kiosk profile cache (states_http already sends Cache-Control: no-store, so that would be a new finding worth routing to Atlas).
